summary: @onereach/rwc-client preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is variable-name obfuscated (_0xXXXX identifiers) and, when Bun is not already on PATH, downloads the Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases URL into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) using a string-array shuffle-decoder (function WV8StW with MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())) and hex/char-code constant tables to reconstruct all strings and destinations at runtime, so its network destinations and behavior are opaque without execution. package.json's `files` allowlist declares only dist/lib/richWebChat.umd.min.js, dist/lib/richWebChat.css, and dist/lib/rwc-client.d.ts; setup.mjs and math_init.js ship at the tarball root outside the declared allowlist and are what preinstall executes. The package is advertised as a browser chat widget (UMD bundle) with no native build requirement that would justify fetching an alternate language runtime and running an obfuscated payload under it at install time. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an obfuscated Node lifecycle script pulls in a runtime and hands it a bundled file so the executed code evades Node-based supply-chain scanning.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
